title: CLIP linked different car classes through shared backgrounds or objects
summary: On UrbanCars, 94.8% of highly similar image pairs from different vehicle classes shared a background or a co-occurring object, compared with 18.1% of random cross-class pairs. Researchers selected the similar pairs using pretrained CLIP features before consulting the dataset’s attribute labels.

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, §4 similarity audit, Table 3 and Figure 2

evidence.tested: The audit compared randomly chosen cross-class training pairs with pairs selected using high cosine similarity in the frozen feature space.
evidence.unknown: The reported proportions concern a dataset constructed with two labeled shortcut attributes and the study’s similarity selection. They do not measure real-world shortcut prevalence.
evidence.ai_role: A frozen pretrained vision encoder determined which cross-class examples were closest without using known shortcut labels; audit labels were applied afterward.
